x: A programme of three events gave only a few of our Juniors a chance to show their merit; but Mewes, Crilly, Keyworth, Dyke, Martin, Chantler and Clements certainly seized the opportunity to show their superiority over the other clubs.
Chantler, Martin and Lindsey are three of our members who seem to be in good form early on. The complete result is appended, giving the times of all members.
Special mention must be made of Chantler and Martin, both having run splendidly over the last lap to finish 12th and 13th. Actually Martin pulled up from 34th position at half-way!
Chantler writes of
Chantler, the new champion, had a ding-dong battle all the way with D. Martin, and it was only in the finishing straight that Chantler forced himself to the front and victory.

In the “Junior” race held at Imber Court a week later, the South London Harriers proved the strongest team and we took third place. Chantler and Martin ran well, with Jordan not far away, but we dropped points in our search for a fourth man.

F., Chantler, Lindsey, Doubleday, and then smiling Syd Warboys. We then indulged in a race of our own to the next vantage point near Tattenham Corner, when we saw that Patience had moved up to 15th Bill Rice 25th, Ring 27th, Martin 32nd, Webb 45th, and then our handicapper 48th (looking as though he…

At the end of 2½ miles Chantler was 13th, Martin 15th, Stimpson 17th, and Chantler 23rd. The two first named put in splendid finishes, and Stimpson found an extra bit to split the Aldershot pack, which incidentally enabled us to win by one point.
Wright, Bayliss, Cotton, Jordan, Harley, Chantler and Walker in particular for their regular weeky contributions to the Football Scheme, and all those others who are assisting in some way or other.

Four of our young milers, Clements, Chantler, Stimpson and Wood competed in an under 20 mile team race at the Enfield A.C. Open Meeting, and although our scoring men finished 4, 5, 6, we were placed second.
Edwards, of Ealing, was placed first in the match, followed by Martin, of ours, Shirley (of Ashcombe) and then Stimpson and Chantler, of ours.
George Chantler (the holder), Dave Martin, Ed Stimpson and Ken Wood were always close together; but in the closing stages Stimpson found a little extra speed to finish nine seconds ahead of Martin.
